metadata.name: Critical Cyber Infrastructure
metadata.description: Public-knowledge locations of internet-critical infrastructure relevant to cyber-threat visualization: DNS root server operators, top internet exchange points (IXPs), hyperscaler cloud regions, and major submarine cable landing hubs. Locations are city-level; multi-site anycast operators are shown at their primary administrative site.
metadata.attribution: ICANN, root-servers.org, PeeringDB, AWS/Azure/GCP region documentation, TeleGeography submarine cable map

properties.name: A Root (Verisign)
properties.description: A root server operated by Verisign with anycast nodes globally; administrative home in Dulles, VA.

properties.name: B Root (USC-ISI)
properties.description: B root operated by USC-ISI from Marina del Rey / Los Angeles, with anycast deployment.

properties.name: C Root (Cogent)
properties.description: C root operated by Cogent with anycast nodes worldwide; administrative HQ in Washington, DC area.

properties.name: D Root (University of Maryland)
properties.description: D root operated by UMD with anycast deployment.

properties.name: I Root (Netnod)
properties.description: I root operated by Netnod from Stockholm, with anycast deployment across 70+ sites.

properties.name: K Root (RIPE NCC)
properties.description: K root operated by RIPE NCC from Amsterdam with anycast deployment across 100+ sites.

properties.name: L Root (ICANN)
properties.description: L root operated by ICANN with the largest anycast deployment of any root operator (200+ sites).

properties.name: M Root (WIDE)
properties.description: M root operated by WIDE Project from Tokyo, with anycast deployment across APAC.

properties.name: DE-CIX Frankfurt
properties.description: World's largest internet exchange by peak traffic (~17 Tbps). Frankfurt is Europe's primary peering hub.

properties.name: AMS-IX Amsterdam
properties.description: Second-largest European IXP. ~12 Tbps peak. Anchor of the Dutch/Northern European peering ecosystem.

properties.name: LINX London
properties.description: UK's primary peering hub, ~7 Tbps peak across LON1/LON2.

properties.name: Equinix Ashburn (NoVA)
properties.description: Densest interconnection campus in the world. Hosts MAE-East, Equinix Internet Exchange, and ~70% of global east-west internet traffic at some hour.

properties.name: JPIX/JPNAP Tokyo
properties.description: Japan's primary peering hub. JPIX and JPNAP collectively anchor East Asian traffic.

properties.name: Equinix Singapore
properties.description: Southeast Asia's primary peering and submarine cable convergence point.

properties.name: MIX Milan
properties.description: Southern European peering hub, primary anchor for Italian and Mediterranean traffic.

properties.name: PTT.br São Paulo (IX.br)
properties.description: Largest IXP in Latin America by peak traffic (~15 Tbps). Anchor of Brazilian peering.

properties.name: AWS us-east-1 (N. Virginia)
properties.description: AWS's largest and oldest region. Single-region outages have historically affected ~30% of internet services.

properties.name: AWS us-west-2 (Oregon)
properties.description: AWS's primary West Coast region; many federal and FedRAMP-high workloads run here.

properties.name: AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland)
properties.description: AWS's primary European region; default for many EU-GDPR-resident workloads.

properties.name: AWS ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo)
properties.description: AWS's primary APAC region serving Japan/Korea finance and gaming workloads.

properties.name: Azure East US (Virginia)
properties.description: Azure's primary East Coast region; co-located with NoVA hyperscaler concentration.

properties.name: Azure West Europe (Netherlands)
properties.description: Azure's primary European hub, located in Amsterdam.

properties.name: GCP us-central1 (Iowa)
properties.description: GCP's primary US region in Council Bluffs, IA.

properties.name: GCP europe-west1 (Belgium)
properties.description: GCP's primary European region in St. Ghislain, Belgium.

properties.name: Cloudflare HQ + Global Anycast
properties.description: Cloudflare global anycast network reaches ~20% of websites. Single-config-deploy outages have caused internet-scale incidents.

properties.name: MAREA Cable Landing (Virginia Beach)
properties.description: US landing of the MAREA trans-Atlantic cable (160 Tbps), connecting Virginia Beach to Bilbao, Spain.

properties.name: MAREA Cable Landing (Bilbao)
properties.description: Spanish landing of the MAREA trans-Atlantic cable.

properties.name: 2Africa Cable Hub (Marseille)
properties.description: Mediterranean hub for the 2Africa cable, the world's longest subsea system (45,000 km around Africa, Middle East, Asia).

properties.name: Fujairah Cable Hub (UAE)
properties.description: Persian Gulf cable convergence point. Critical chokepoint for Asia-Europe-Africa traffic; vulnerable to anchor cuts in the Red Sea.

properties.name: Toucheng Cable Landing (Taiwan)
properties.description: Primary Taiwan submarine cable landing. Strategic chokepoint repeatedly affected by cable damage incidents 2022–2026.

properties.name: DigiCert (Lehi, UT)
properties.description: Largest issuer of EV/OV certificates. Single-vendor outage cascaded across HTTPS verification 2024.

properties.name: Let's Encrypt (ISRG)
properties.description: Free CA issuing 5M+ certificates daily. Underpins ~50% of public HTTPS certificates by issuance volume.
